evidence: The containing symbol has a long roof and two descending legs, with two overtraced loops on the left. These support the existing pi/calligraphic-E alternatives; there is no distinct new G bowl and inward crossbar that would settle it as calligraphic G. The raised barred L and lower L/K remain clear. The following comma is already in the page text.
outcome: Retain the existing whole-formula uncertainty and its preferred pi reading.

evidence: Below ou, the struck word leaves low initial strokes, a rounded o, an open c and separate high marks toward the ending. It is longer than the proposed preci fragment and lacks a secure initial p descender. The cancellation prevents a complete lexical resolution, while the live plutôt and comma are clear.
outcome: Retain the doubtful deleted associés; no doubt is resolved.

evidence: The inserted glyph has a flat roof and two straight short legs, followed by a separate hyphen. This is the same flat-roof form already recorded for the page's pi notation; in this small insertion the ink does not establish a separate capital group symbol. The lower curve is the insertion leader.
outcome: Retain pi-conjugaison, using the established notation where the two handwritten cases have the same outline.

evidence: The first word has a low double-humped entry followed by a short e return. Convaincre has the open c/o opening, angular v, separate i dot and compact cre ending, followed by a tall d and u. The first low word is compatible with the page's compressed me form and has no additional letter supporting une.
outcome: Retain me convaincre du; the independent alternative does not unsettle the clear verb.

evidence: The initial doubtful verb has only low connected strokes and no tall medial t required by montrer. After the dash and que, ce is separate from the following s/o/n/t run; there is no apostrophe to make c'est. The word beginning with the deep j continues through the flattened ment tail, not just juste. The final accented à and sous- are visible.
outcome: Retain énoncer|annoncer, ce sont justement, and the written sous- ending.

evidence: A tall initial stroke and a small low curve survive at the left; the middle and final strokes merge with the broad horizontal and diagonal cancellation. They permit the earlier tout and the independent les, but neither word is fully recoverable. The cancellation is certain.
outcome: Add les as an explicit alternative within the existing lexical doubt, without a new correction against C.

evidence: The lower crossed relation retains a horizontal trace and a bent right-hand end, so a tentative right arrow remains a defensible candidate rather than wholly unassignable ink. The live membership sign sits above it. The large X has curved arms with extra crossing strokes and terminal returns, matching the fraktur form used for this valuation-space notation on these leaves; it is distinct from plain X.
outcome: Retain the existing doubtful deleted arrow, raised membership sign and fraktur X.

evidence: The baseline word at the left has a p descender, small a and s return (pas). Above it is the looped d with low e and a leader into the gap before centre. Thus the raised addition is de, not a lower pro prefix. After centre, the long low joins belong to dans. The cancellation covers X, the oblique difference mark and old U; the following U, three points and closing parenthesis are live.
outcome: Retain the existing words, deletion scope and insertion attachment.

evidence: The l has a closed upper loop and heavily retraced stem and foot. Its transverse top and basal strokes admit an overwritten I, but no separate cancelling stroke or independently legible earlier letter can be isolated. One apostrophe and one ens. group follow.
outcome: Retain one live l'ens.; describe the retracing without inventing a recoverable earlier I state.

final: D_J^*=\{x\in X\mid I(x)=J\}=\overbrace{\bigcap_{j\in J}D_j}^{\Delta_J}-\bigcup_{i\in I\unsure{\setminus|-}J}\Delta_J\cap D_i
evidence: The starred D_J, set braces, triangular Delta labels, overbrace, large subtraction stroke and final D_i are visible. The argument of I uses the same small loop-and-return x as elsewhere on the page. Between I and J in the union bound, however, the very short stroke descends only shallowly: it can be a compact slash or a slanted minus. The first reading's unqualified slash was too confident.
outcome: Retain the formula and add a local slash/minus doubt in its union bound.

evidence: The first D has braced i; the right-hand subtraction slash, enclosing parenthesis, union and j not-equal i bound are visible. The compressed interior has D_i and a cap-like join followed by a last D. No separate final j can be isolated between that D and the closing parenthesis, although the crowded terminal curve could hide it. The point is independent.
outcome: Prefer the visible term without a supplied final index, retaining the indexed alternative as unresolved within the existing whole-term doubt.

evidence: Si, the tall-stem d, equality, card J and comma are clear. The following low run has a slight rounded entry and shallow terminal bend, but its o and n cannot be separated securely from a single cursive stroke. The earlier resolution of C's on mark is therefore withdrawn.
outcome: Restore uncertainty on on; keep the ink in the transcription without resolving it from the sentence.

evidence: A separate short wavy glyph stands above the end of codim, lower than the mathematical line above and independent of the régulier insertion leader. Its two low turns support a raised contraction n, although its letter shape is compressed. The following baseline d has a round bowl and high ascender.
outcome: Restore the omitted raised contraction mark as a doubtful n; retain the baseline d.

evidence: The opening has two separate ticks. At the right the dark closing mark has adjoining projections but their overlap prevents confidently counting one versus two strokes. The p descender, looped l and crossed x establish simplexe.
outcome: Retain double closing ticks as preferred and mark their count uncertain.

final: \margin{il vaut mieux définir $D_J$ comme \uline{\unsure{sous-schém.|sous-schéma}} comme $\subset\bigcap_{j\in J}D_j$, et définir son \uline{support} comme $\{x\in X\mid I(x)=J\}$} \tag{36}
evidence: The first symbol has a rounded D bowl, not the triangular Delta of the main display. The low joins after it support one comme; no separately spaced un is secure. The underlined sous-schém group ends in compressed minims and an independent dot, so the abbreviated ending is preferred but remains uncertain. A separate open inclusion curve stands before the intersection. The number (36) is upright in the original and becomes tilted when the oblique writing is levelled; it aligns with the main display and is not part of the marginal sentence. After the marginal formula a separate comma precedes et. In the later underlined word, the two deep p descenders and terminal t support support, without a hyphen or the longer ouvert sequence. The final relation has two heavy parallel bars and no enclosing curve, so equality remains the reading.
outcome: Restore display number 36, remove its marginal duplication, add the omitted inclusion sign, retain a short-form ending doubt, and resolve the underlined noun to support. Keep D_J, the repeated comme and final equality.

evidence: The thin foliation has two sloping-entry uprights around the double-curved 3. Both readings give 131; only the margin wrapper differs.
outcome: Retain 131 in the existing margin wrapper.

evidence: The glyph is a closed oval crossed by a long stem extending above and well below it to a hooked foot. This is the same closed-loop phi form compared across the other leaves, for which the transcription consistently uses phi; there is no distinct open cursive varphi form here.
outcome: Retain phi for the written empty-set glyph; no normalization to an empty-set symbol.
